reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that off-ball defensive actions—particularly those that block passing lanes—are not captured by conventional metrics. The paper introduces a framework where a defender's impact is measured by computing the probability of blocking a pass at any location using time-to-intercept and estimated ball travel time. This leads to a probabilistic model of cover shadows. Threat reduction index is derived by comparing the total threat of possible passes in a game state with and without a specific defender. This requires modeling pass completion likelihoods and aggregating them over all potential passes. The framework leverages StatsBomb 360 data to provide spatial context around events, enabling precise tracking of player positions during key moments. The dual nature of this approach lies in its ability to quantify both individual defensive impact and collective team-level disruption. Failure modes include misclassification of defenders due to inaccurate tracking data or oversimplification of pass likelihoods. The method also assumes static threat models, which may not reflect dynamic tactical shifts during play.
